# Bundled bot browser: upstream provenance and notices

The desktop application ships two separate components:

- **agent-browser 0.37.0** on macOS and Linux, official Vercel release executables from
  <https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser/releases/tag/v0.37.0>.
  Its Apache-2.0 license is included as `agent-browser-LICENSE.txt`.
  The bundled axe-core code's upstream license and third-party notices are
  included as `LICENSE-axe-core.txt` and `LICENSE-axe-core-THIRD-PARTY.txt`.
  These files match the `v0.37.0` source tag (unchanged from `v0.36.0`); there
  is no root-level NOTICE in that tag. All six official macOS/Linux binaries
  were downloaded and their SHA-256 digests checked against GitHub's release
  metadata on 2026-09-08.
- **Windows exception: agent-browser 0.36.0-omb.1** is an OpenMausBot vendor
  build, not an official or unmodified Vercel executable. It starts from exact
  v0.36.0 commit `eb05921bad874cd2a1b4fa5d1149f1ed26576cae` and carries
  the Windows handle-inheritance fix contributed by `holny` in upstream
  [PR1781](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser/pull/1781), commit
  `81a98c349d04195396ffae6898bd375ad64280de`, plus OpenMausBot's Windows-only
  `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` flag for Chrome children and a native console regression test
  in candidate revision `0.36.0-omb.2`. The release resolver retains `0.36.0-omb.1`
  until the candidate passes native checks and its published digest is reviewed.
  The separate MCP output-reader
  rewrite is deliberately excluded. `agent-browser-windows-stdio.patch`
  includes the exact changes and modification notices, plus package-version
  metadata; dependency versions remain locked. The original Apache and axe
  notices remain unchanged. `scripts/build-windows-browser-vendor.mjs` pins
  the source archive, patch, Rust 1.97.1, pnpm 11.1.3 and Windows GNU target,
  builds the real upstream dashboard, and emits executable and build-input
  digests in `provenance.json`. Native Windows cold-start and close/reopen
  checks are required before those executable bytes are published and pinned.
  Upstream 0.37.0 does not include that fix; keep this tested Windows build
  until an updated official or backported release passes those native checks.
  Both Windows revisions also start a session's daemon with its stderr piped to
  the short-lived CLI call that spawned it (`ensure_daemon` in
  `cli/src/connection.rs`). Once that call exits, the daemon's next stderr
  write fails and panics; it writes one when more than 4096 CDP events queue
  up, so a page load of ~600+ requests breaks the session. The server works
  around it with `server/browser-daemon.ts`, which starts each session's daemon
  itself with stderr on the NUL device. A vendor fix, `0.36.0-omb.3`, fits the
  existing flow; nothing is downloaded outside the reviewed Linux runner:
  1. On that runner, extract the pinned source archive and apply the current
     patch, as `scripts/build-windows-browser-vendor.mjs` does, in a git
     working tree.
  2. In the Windows branch of `ensure_daemon`, spawn the daemon with
     `.stderr(Stdio::null())` (or a log file under the socket directory)
     instead of `Stdio::piped()`, and drop or adapt the code that reads that
     pipe for startup errors. Add a `// Modified by OpenMausBot` notice and set
     `0.36.0-omb.3` in `cli/Cargo.toml` and `cli/Cargo.lock`.
  3. Regenerate `agent-browser-windows-stdio.patch` with `git diff` against
     the base commit, keeping the header notice, then update
     `WINDOWS_VENDOR_VERSION`, `WINDOWS_VENDOR_PATCH_SHA256` (SHA-256 of the
     new patch) and the provenance `scope` in that script, and its test.
  4. Run `node scripts/build-windows-browser-vendor.mjs --output
     /absolute/new/dir`; it records the executable digest in
     `provenance.json`.
  5. On native Windows, point `OMB_AGENT_BROWSER_PATH` at the candidate and
     run the cold-start and close/reopen checks plus
     `server/browser-daemon.e2e.test.ts` and
     `scripts/testing/session-daemon.e2e.test.ts`, once with the server's
     daemon start disabled, to prove the build alone survives the 1,200-module
     page.
  6. Publish the executable and pin its URL, size and SHA-256 in the `win32-x64`
     entry of `server/browser-engine-release.ts`.
- **Chromium Headless Shell 153.0.8010.47**, Google's official
  `chrome-headless-shell` assets published through Chrome for Testing:
  <https://googlechromelabs.github.io/chrome-for-testing/153.0.8010.47.json>.
  The complete archive tree is retained, including `ABOUT` and
  `LICENSE.headless_shell`. The latter includes the Chromium BSD notice
  (including its binary-redistribution conditions) and the complete
  target-specific third-party license texts generated by Chromium's build.
  Source and license-generation rule:
  <https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/153.0.8010.47/headless/BUILD.gn>.

The bundled browser is the headless automation build, **not the full Google
Chrome distribution**. In particular, it does not bundle the proprietary
Widevine content-decryption module. The Apache-2.0 license in the
Chrome-for-Testing dashboard repository does not license Chrome executables;
we do not use it as the browser's license. Upstream's ABOUT notice and its
Chrome terms reference are retained without modification:
<https://www.google.com/chrome/terms/>.

All five archive sizes and SHA-256 digests were calculated from the vendor
downloads on 2026-09-16 and pinned in `server/browser-bundle-release.ts`.
Engine asset pins are reused from `server/browser-engine-release.ts`.
Preparation checks the exact archive bytes on every run, including cached
downloads, then records a complete file/symlink inventory. Missing, modified,
or incomplete staged resources fail the pre-signing package check.

Archives and extracted binaries are generated build output, not git content.
Set `OMB_BROWSER_ARCHIVE_DIR` to a directory of reviewed vendor assets for an
offline build; cached bytes are still verified. Browser dependencies are
updated through reviewed OpenMausBot releases, not a silent browser updater.

On macOS, release signing applies OpenMausBot's Developer ID to native
executables and libraries after validating the upstream bytes. The original
notices remain intact. Packaged browser profiles, cookies and downloads are
never included here; those belong in the user's isolated bot data directory.

Google, Chromium and Vercel are their owners' names; their inclusion does not
imply endorsement of OpenMausBot. This provenance record is not legal advice
or a replacement for the included upstream licenses.
